newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey clears U.S. wheat, to ease import limits.
newsitem.headline: Turkey clears U.S. wheat, to ease import limits.

text.p: Turkey has cleared cargoes of U.S. wheat it was holding up on grounds they might contain ergot fungus and a new regulation will ease a zero-tolerance policy through a government decree expected to come out soon, officials said.
"As of last night we allowed the U.S. wheat cargoes to come into Turkey," said a senior agricultural ministry official, who declined to be named.
"Instead of a zero-tolerance limit, we will from now seek a 0.02 percent limit for ergot disease in imported wheat," he told Reuters.
He said a government decree amending an article of the present Farm Quarantine Act was prepared and sent to prime ministry for final approval.
"The new policy may come out in the Official Gazette either later today or tomorrow," he said. He did not give other information.

Officials said some 60,000 to 65,000 tonnes of U.S. milling wheat imported by private millers and international traders have been held up at Tekirdag, Derince, Izmir and Mersin ports for about two weeks for checks against the ergot fungus.
A zero-tolerance policy defined in the country's Farm Quarantine Act, actually designed for seed wheat only, was mistakenly applied to milling wheat, importers said.
But Turkish farmers, traders and millers as well as U.S. officials said no country in the world can guarantee a zero-tolerance for ergot fungus.
Another piece of Turkish legislation, called Food Act, allows 0.1 percent of ergot in imported wheat.

A United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) official said on Monday Turkish agricultural ministry had told them there was a misundertanding in the legislations applied and a new regulation to correct the issue was being prepared.
Traders said some 100,000 tonnes of milling wheat, including the cargoes presently waiting at the ports, were heading for Turkey from the United States.
